newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium may move above $2,000 in 1997 - GNI. [CORRECTED 17:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Aluminium may move above $2,000 in 1997 - GNI. [CORRECTED 17:52 GMT]

text.p: Three months LME aluminium prices are expected to average $1,600 a tonne and possibly peak above $2,000 in 1997, brokers GNI said in their latest commodity perspective report.
While there is still the question of idled capacity being brought on line, the recent fall in prices has served as a strong warning to producers not to increase production too soon.
GNI said that excess production will only be brought on line when prices can justify it and London Metal Exchange (LME) stocks are at dramatically low levels.
Offtake is likely to grow from 19.9 million tonnes in 1996 to 20.47 million tonnes in 1997, an increase of 2.9 percent.
In 1996 prices are likely to average around $1,500.

"We do not rule out a brief move to $1,300 at some stage in the early part of next year," analyst Lawrence Eagles said, quoting a previous report written in 1995. (Corrects to add reference to previous report and make clear that the move below $1,300 refers to 1996)

The world aluminium market is likely to be in relative balance in 1997. GNI said the market can look forward to primary aluminium production increasing to 20.355 million tonnes in 1997 from 19.62 million tonnes in 1996, an increase of 3.7 percent.
